title: Principality of Polotsky
capsule: The Principality of Polotsk (Полацк) was one of the earliest and most independent of the Kievan Rus principalities, centred on the upper Western Dvina River in present-day Belarus. Under Vseslav the Sorcerer (r. 1044–1101) it reached its greatest extent, briefly seizing Novgorod in 1066 and fighting a famous drawn battle at the Nemiga River against Yaroslav's sons in 1067. The principality maintained a separate Rurikid branch distinct from the Kiev line throughout the period of Rus fragmentation, resisting absorption into neighbouring principalities until the Mongol invasions of the 1240s effectively ended its independent significance.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory along the Western Dvina is well established from chronicle sources; outer boundaries fluctuated with raids and sub-divisions and are approximately reconstructed.
